sharedDecisions.note: Decisions are deployed ONCE and WITHOUT an Organization. Every businessRuleTask in this bundle carries camunda:decisionRefTenantId="${null}", so a tenant-scoped process resolves the SHARED, untenanted decision. Setting the Organization field when importing these — the natural thing to do, since the BPMN beside them is tenant-scoped — deploys them where the engine will not look, and every process fails at its first business rule task with "no decision definition deployed with key 'X' and tenant-id 'null'".

external.zorgtoeslag_resultaat: Ships with the zorgtoeslag rules set, not with this bundle: it lives in a 23-decision file (def_zorgtoeslag_temporal_demo) with its own lifecycle. Declared here so a stack rebuilt from this manifest knows it is required, and where it does NOT come from.

sharedDecisions.source: Downloaded from the untenanted decision definitions deployed on operaton.open-regels.nl, the same engine the ACC backend uses — the convention the Thuisbatterij bundle set. Verified 22 September 2026: all seven keys present there, every one with tenantId null. The three heusden/ decision files are the exception: they are byte-identical copies of examples/organizations/heusden/, which is where that bundle is authored (example-fixture-parity.test.ts enforces the copy).

subProcesses.source: based on packages/frontend/public/examples/flevoland/TreeFellingPermitSubProcess.bpmn, renamed to TreeFellingPermitSubProcessE2E (id + filename) to give this fixture its own Operaton key, distinct from the seeded example — LDE's own catalog otherwise conflates the two by shared process id, silently redeploying stale content; called via AwbShellProcess's callActivity calledElement="TreeFellingPermitSubProcessE2E" — deployed together with the shell in one LDE Modeler action, not separately

taken from the flevoland-tenant bundle deployed on operaton.open-regels.nl (deployment 8803912d, 2026-09-21), and since #192 also the authored copy in examples/organizations/flevoland/thuisbatterij/, which replaced the drifted -main/-subprocess pair that used to live there (example-fixture-parity.test.ts keeps it identical to public/examples). Every businessRuleTask carries camunda:decisionRefTenantId="${null}" so the tenant-scoped process resolves the SHARED, untenanted DMNs; the deployed copy pinned decisionRefTenantId="46" instead, which tied it to one organisation's tenant. RechtEnHoogteSubsidieThuisbatterij.dmn holds all six decisions and MUST be deployed WITHOUT a tenant-id.

heusden.source: examples/organizations/heusden/swimlanes-for-rba/HeusdenpasAanvraagProcess.bpmn, byte-identical (example-fixture-parity.test.ts). Unlike the flevoland and toeslagen fixtures it keeps its real keys and carries no E2E labels: ronl-business-api's required-processes.ts expects the same keys on every tier, and a byte-identical copy cannot go stale, which is what the E2E suffix guards against (#274).
